text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Whither Romanian economy ? West or south ?, paper asks.
- Commodity exchange should have its own regulating body, paper says.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- The depreciation of the leu currency anticipates an unemployment rate of up to 16 percent.
- Editorial writes about "the two faces" of official statistics.
- Paper prints commodities import and export regime in 1997.
- Transport Minister Traian Basescu says in interview that the state will support the national airline Tarom SA and that rise in transport tariffs is meant to modernise facilities.
- Leading Romanian politicians on the issue of the sale of land to foreign investors.
- The paper prints targets for privatisation and restructuring involving Romanian state companies which it says were "tabled to the government by international lending institutions."
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Leaders of the ruling centrist coalition gave Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea their unonditional support for the government's reform package, during meeting at presidential Palace late on Wednesday, paper says.
- The U.S. dollar fetches 7,500 lei at money changing bureaux.
- Prices of imported cigarettes went up by 25 percent.
- Former senior finance ministry official says that hike of telephone tariffs reflects attempt to boost profit for Romtelecom RA phone utility ahead of its privatisation.
ADEVARUL
- Interview with Sorin Dimitriu, newly appointed president of the State Ownership Fund, who says big loss-making industries will be streamlined.
- The central bank (BNR) jacked up rate on one-week refinancing credits to 125.45 percent, from previous 90 percent, while halving lei on offer to 600 billion, in a bid to mop up excess liquidities.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Marcel Dinu was appointed ambassador to Moldova.
- French President Francois Chirac expected to address parliament during visit to Romania.
- Senate chairman Petre Roman denies saying the ruling coalition is threatened by disagreements among its members.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Editorialist Ion Cristoiu, director of daily nespaper Evenimentul Zilei, plans to resign, the paper says.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
